_comment: ANNOTATIONS for the geostationary weather list, not the list itself. geo.py lists every geostationary object in Celestrak's weather group and computes its longitude from its own elements; a row here only adds what we know about one. `tle` is a case-insensitive PREFIX matched against the TLE name; the longest match wins. Do not put a longitude here: slots get reassigned, and the computed one is the truth. Frequencies in MHz. Every `source` says where the number came from and when.

downlinks.name: HRIT/EMWIN
downlinks.what: 400 kbps BPSK, linear polarisation. Full-disc and regional imagery plus EMWIN text. The one a 1 m dish and an RTL-SDR can decode.

downlinks.name: GRB
downlinks.what: Full-resolution rebroadcast, dual circular polarisation, about 31 Mbps. Needs a much larger dish and a wideband receiver.

satellites.note: Operational GOES-East since April 2025. HRIT needs roughly a 1 m dish or a WiFi grid antenna, an L-band LNA with a filter, and an SDR; SatDump or goestools decode it.
satellites.source: Frequencies: NOAA HRIT/EMWIN page and GOES-R fact sheet, checked 2026-11-16. Role: from memory, confirmed by the computed slot near 75.2 W.

satellites.note: Operational GOES-West. Low in the south-west from the US east coast, so trees and buildings matter more than for GOES-East.
satellites.source: Frequencies: NOAA HRIT/EMWIN page and GOES-R fact sheet, checked 2026-11-16. Role: from memory, confirmed by the computed slot near 137 W.
